**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8949664, Reactome:R-HSA-9837999)

This disruption leads to the accumulation of misfolded proteins within mitochondria, ultimately causing neurodegeneration and manifesting as spinocerebellar ataxia and optic atrophy.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in AFG3L2 with a demonstrable gain-of-function effect or a distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathway for each disease would falsify this shared loss-of-function mechanism. _(variant: A common loss-of-function variant in AFG3L2 (e.g., allele frequency > 0.01 in gnomAD) would suggest incomplete penetrance or a different underlying mechanism.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of AFG3L2 in mitochondrial protein homeostasis offers a potential therapeutic target for both spinocerebellar ataxia type 28 and optic atrophy 12, possibly through strategies aimed at restoring mitochondrial function or enhancing protein degradation pathways.
